sample_unit: standardized TMD patient-friendly questions per chatbot

links.outcome: Proportion of chatbot-cited references that were hallucinated (not authentic or retrievable)
links.effect: GPT-4 47.2% hallucinated references, Gemini Pro 18.8%, DeepSeek-V3 10.1% (P < .001).
links.quote: The transformer-based autoregressive model produced the highest proportion of hallucinated references (47.2%), compared with the multimodal transformer (18.8%) and the mixture-of-experts transformer (10.1%) (P < .001).

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to patient-friendly TMD questions (Flesch-Kincaid)
links.effect: Most readable model (DeepSeek-V3) had Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease 28.47 and Grade Level 12.19 (P < .001), which is difficult, college-level text.
links.quote: The mixture-of-experts transformer provided the most readable content (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease = 28.47; Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level = 12.19; P < .001).

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on accuracy, readability, empathy, and hallucinated references when answering TMD-related questions, without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
